name: Medicine (MD/DO student)
scope: Takes a focused or complete history, performs a physical examination, orders and interprets investigations, forms a differential diagnosis and a management plan under supervision.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
wrapUp.placeholder: e.g. 59M with HFrEF presenting with early satiety and weight loss...

wrapUp.label: Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: History taking, clinical reasoning, differential diagnosis, safe management, shared decision making.

name: Family Medicine
scope: Provides first-contact and continuing care for patients of all ages by video: undifferentiated complaints, chronic disease follow-up, preventive care and screening, medication management, and coordination of referrals. Decides what can be managed remotely and what needs an in-person visit.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, health maintenance, safety-netting and follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Whole-person history, prioritising multiple problems, preventive care, shared decision making, safety-netting, continuity.

name: Internal Medicine / Hospital Medicine
scope: Evaluates adults with complex or multi-system illness, reconciles medications, interprets investigations, and manages transitions of care. By video this is typically a post-discharge follow-up, a pre-admission evaluation or a complex chronic disease visit.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Problem-based assessment (each active problem with reasoning)
Plan by problem: investigations, treatment changes, follow-up and return precautions

rubricEmphasis: Clinical reasoning across multiple problems, medication reconciliation, interpretation of results, safe transitions of care.

name: Emergency Medicine
scope: Runs virtual urgent-care and tele-triage visits: rapidly identifies or excludes life-threatening conditions, risk-stratifies, and decides disposition (self-care, urgent in-person assessment, or call an ambulance now). Gives clear return precautions.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Medical decision making: must-not-miss diagnoses considered and how each was addressed
Disposition (home, in-person today, EMS) with reasoning
Treatment and return precautions given

rubricEmphasis: Recognition of red flags, focused efficient history, risk stratification, safe disposition, explicit return precautions.

name: Pediatrics
scope: Cares for infants, children and adolescents by video with a parent or caregiver present: acute illness, growth and development, feeding, behaviour, immunisation and anticipatory guidance. Takes history from the caregiver and, where age-appropriate, the child; offers confidential time to adolescents.
noteFormat: SOAP (with growth, development and immunization status)

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential, including growth, development and hydration status where relevant
Plan: investigations, weight-based treatment, caregiver education, return precautions

rubricEmphasis: Caregiver-inclusive history, developmental and growth assessment, weight-based dosing, safeguarding awareness, clear advice for parents.

name: Cardiology
scope: Assesses and follows patients with heart disease by video: chest pain and dyspnoea evaluation, heart failure, arrhythmia, hypertension, lipid and risk-factor management. Reviews ECGs, echocardiograms, device and home-monitoring data and titrates guideline-directed therapy.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Cardiac assessment: diagnosis, functional class, risk stratification and reasoning
Plan: testing, medication titration, lifestyle advice, follow-up and warning signs

rubricEmphasis: Symptom characterisation, cardiovascular risk stratification, ECG/echo interpretation, guideline-directed therapy, adherence counselling.

name: Medical Oncology
scope: Discusses cancer diagnoses, staging and treatment options, monitors patients on systemic therapy for toxicity, and leads goals-of-care conversations. Tele-visits include results disclosure, treatment planning, on-treatment toxicity checks and survivorship follow-up.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Oncologic assessment: diagnosis, stage, performance status, treatment toxicity and urgent issues
Plan: treatment decisions, supportive care, what the patient was told and understood, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Delivering serious news (SPIKES), toxicity grading, recognising oncologic emergencies, eliciting values, shared decision making.

name: Hematology
scope: Evaluates and manages blood disorders: anaemia, abnormal counts, bleeding and clotting disorders, anticoagulation, sickle cell disease and haematologic malignancy follow-up. By video the work is history, interpretation of blood counts and smears reported in the record, and treatment decisions.
encounterTypes: new consultation for abnormal blood count

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Bleeding and thrombosis history, systematic CBC interpretation, anticoagulation safety, family history, explaining results clearly.

name: Neurology
scope: Assesses headache, seizure, weakness, tremor, memory and sensory complaints. Localises the lesion from history and a camera-guided neurological examination, recognises emergencies such as stroke, and manages chronic conditions such as epilepsy, migraine, MS and Parkinson disease.
noteFormat: Neurology consult note (history, exam, localisation, plan)

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Localisation, differential diagnosis and reasoning
Plan: investigations, treatment, driving/safety advice, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Precise symptom timeline, remote neurological examination, localisation, recognising stroke and other emergencies, safety counselling.

name: Psychiatry
scope: Conducts psychiatric interviews and mental status examinations, assesses risk of harm to self or others, formulates a diagnosis, and plans treatment with medication and psychotherapy referral. Telepsychiatry includes intake evaluations, medication management and crisis assessment.
noteFormat: Psychiatric evaluation (HPI, MSE, risk assessment, formulation, plan)

wrapUp.label: Mental status examination: key findings
Risk assessment (suicide, harm to others, self-neglect) and safety plan
Diagnostic formulation and differential
Plan: medication, psychotherapy, monitoring, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Therapeutic alliance, mental status examination, direct and sensitive suicide risk assessment, biopsychosocial formulation, safety planning.

name: Obstetrics and Gynecology
scope: Provides prenatal and postpartum care, contraception and preconception counselling, and evaluation of gynaecologic complaints such as abnormal bleeding, pelvic pain and menopausal symptoms. By video, identifies which concerns need same-day in-person assessment.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential (include gestational age / obstetric history where relevant)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Sensitive sexual and reproductive history, obstetric warning signs, trauma-informed and non-judgmental counselling, patient autonomy.

name: General Surgery
scope: Evaluates surgical problems and operative candidacy, obtains informed consent, and follows patients after operations. Tele-visits are pre-operative consultations, post-operative wound and recovery checks, and triage of possible complications.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Surgical assessment: diagnosis, indication or post-operative course, complications considered
Plan: operative or non-operative management, consent points discussed, wound care, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Operative risk assessment, informed consent, recognising post-operative complications, camera-guided wound assessment, clear instructions.

name: Orthopedic Surgery
scope: Assesses musculoskeletal injury and joint disease, reviews imaging, and advises on operative versus non-operative treatment. By video: mechanism-of-injury history, patient-performed range-of-motion and special tests, fracture and post-operative follow-up.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: imaging, operative vs non-operative treatment, weight-bearing and activity advice, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Mechanism of injury, guided remote musculoskeletal examination, imaging interpretation, neurovascular red flags, functional goals.

name: Anesthesiology
scope: Performs pre-anaesthesia assessment by video: medical and anaesthetic history, airway and cardiopulmonary risk, functional capacity, medication and fasting instructions, and discussion of the anaesthetic plan and its risks.

wrapUp.label: Risk assessment: ASA class, airway, cardiopulmonary and other anaesthetic risks
Anaesthetic plan and alternatives discussed
Pre-operative instructions: fasting, which medications to hold or continue, further testing

rubricEmphasis: Systematic pre-operative risk assessment, airway history, perioperative medication management, plain-language consent.

name: Radiology
scope: Patient-facing radiology consultation: explains imaging findings and what they do and do not mean, reviews appropriateness of requested imaging, screens for contrast and procedure risks, and consents patients for image-guided procedures. Does not take over management from the referring clinician.
noteFormat: Radiology consult note / structured report impression

wrapUp.label: Key imaging findings and impression in your own words
What you told the patient and how you checked understanding
Recommendations: further imaging or procedure, safety precautions, communication to the referring clinician

rubricEmphasis: Explaining findings without jargon, communicating uncertainty and incidental findings, contrast and radiation safety, consent.

name: Pathology
scope: Patient-facing pathology consultation: explains a biopsy, cytology or laboratory report (what was examined, what the diagnosis and its terms mean, what remains uncertain) and transfusion or blood-bank issues. Coordinates with the treating team and does not make treatment recommendations beyond scope.

wrapUp.label: Diagnosis and key report elements in your own words
What the patient understood and the questions they asked
Additional testing recommended and communication back to the treating team

rubricEmphasis: Translating technical reports into plain language, honesty about uncertainty, staying within scope, handing back to the treating clinician.

name: Dermatology
scope: Evaluates rashes, lesions, hair and nail disorders by video and submitted photographs: lesion history, camera-guided skin inspection, recognising lesions that need in-person dermoscopy or biopsy, and managing chronic conditions such as acne, eczema and psoriasis.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment: morphology described, differential diagnosis and reasoning
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Describing morphology, limits of teledermatology, skin cancer red flags, treatment vehicle and quantity instructions, quality-of-life impact.

name: Endocrinology
scope: Manages diabetes, thyroid, adrenal, pituitary, bone and other hormonal disorders. Tele-visits centre on reviewing glucose data and laboratory trends, adjusting insulin and other therapy, and counselling on self-management.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: therapy adjustment (with doses), monitoring, hypoglycaemia safety, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Interpreting glucose and hormone data, safe dose titration, hypoglycaemia awareness, self-management support.

name: Gastroenterology and Hepatology
scope: Evaluates digestive and liver complaints: reflux, abdominal pain, altered bowel habit, GI bleeding, abnormal liver tests, inflammatory bowel disease. By video, takes the history, reviews labs and endoscopy or imaging reports, and decides on endoscopy and treatment.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Alarm-feature screening, bowel and dietary history taken without embarrassment, interpreting liver tests, endoscopy indications.

name: Nephrology
scope: Manages chronic kidney disease, electrolyte disorders, hypertension, glomerular disease and dialysis planning. Tele-visits review kidney function trends, blood pressure logs and medications, and prepare patients for kidney replacement decisions.
encounterTypes: new consultation for abnormal kidney function

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: medication changes (renal dosing, nephrotoxin avoidance), monitoring, kidney replacement planning, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Interpreting eGFR and albuminuria trends, nephrotoxin review, blood pressure and volume assessment, modality education.

name: Pulmonology and Critical Care
scope: Evaluates cough, breathlessness, asthma, COPD, interstitial lung disease, sleep-disordered breathing and lung nodules, and follows patients after critical illness. Reviews spirometry, imaging and home oximetry, and optimises inhaled therapy.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Dyspnoea characterisation, exposure and smoking history, spirometry interpretation, inhaler technique, exacerbation action plans.

name: Infectious Disease
scope: Evaluates complex or recurrent infections, fever, and HIV, hepatitis and travel-related illness; oversees antimicrobial selection and outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. Takes detailed exposure, travel and sexual histories.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, antimicrobial choice with dose and duration, monitoring, prevention and follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Exposure and sexual history without judgment, antimicrobial stewardship, adherence, confidentiality and stigma awareness.

name: Rheumatology
scope: Evaluates joint pain, autoimmune and inflammatory disease, and monitors immunosuppressive therapy. By video: pattern-of-joint-involvement history, patient-guided joint examination, interpretation of serologies and safety laboratory monitoring.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Inflammatory versus mechanical pattern, extra-articular features, serology interpretation, DMARD safety monitoring, function.

name: Geriatric Medicine
scope: Performs comprehensive geriatric assessment of older adults, often with a family caregiver on the call: cognition, mood, falls, function, continence, polypharmacy and goals of care. Prioritises what matters most to the patient.
noteFormat: Comprehensive geriatric assessment (4Ms: what Matters, Medication, Mentation, Mobility)

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Geriatric assessment: cognition, mood, function, falls, medications, what matters to the patient
Plan: deprescribing, safety measures, caregiver support, referrals, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Functional and cognitive assessment, deprescribing, involving caregivers while respecting autonomy, goals-aligned care.

name: Palliative Care
scope: Assesses and treats pain and other symptoms in serious illness, explores understanding of illness, values and goals, supports advance care planning and caregivers. Tele-visits are symptom reviews, goals-of-care conversations and family meetings.

wrapUp.label: Symptom assessment (pain and other symptoms, severity, current regimen)
Patient's understanding of illness, values, goals and stated preferences
Plan: symptom regimen (with doses), advance care planning, caregiver support, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Serious-illness communication, responding to emotion, safe opioid prescribing, eliciting values, caregiver support.

name: Urology
scope: Evaluates urinary symptoms, haematuria, kidney stones, erectile and sexual dysfunction, prostate concerns including PSA results, and incontinence. By video: history, symptom scores, review of urinalysis and imaging, and counselling on options.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Sensitive urinary and sexual history, haematuria red flags, validated symptom scores, shared decision making on screening and treatment.

name: Ophthalmology
scope: Triages and follows eye disease by video: red eye, vision change, flashes and floaters, post-operative checks, glaucoma and diabetic eye disease follow-up. Recognises sight-threatening emergencies that need same-day in-person examination.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: urgency of in-person examination, treatment, drop instructions, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Red-flag screening for sight-threatening disease, limits of remote eye examination, drop adherence and technique.

name: Otolaryngology (ENT)
scope: Evaluates ear, nose, throat, voice, hearing, balance and neck-mass complaints. By video: focused history, camera inspection of the oropharynx and neck, review of audiograms and imaging, and identification of head and neck cancer red flags.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Head and neck red flags, vertigo characterisation, audiogram interpretation, airway warning signs.

name: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
scope: Leads rehabilitation after stroke, spinal cord injury, brain injury, amputation and musculoskeletal or pain conditions. Assesses impairment, function and participation, manages spasticity, pain and bowel/bladder issues, and coordinates the therapy team and equipment.
encounterTypes: post-stroke or spinal cord injury follow-up
noteFormat: Physiatry consult note (impairments, function, rehabilitation plan)

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions; medical complications
Rehabilitation plan: therapy prescriptions, medications, equipment, functional goals, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Function-centred history, goal setting, interprofessional coordination, preventing secondary complications.

name: Physician Assistant / Associate
scope: Takes histories, examines, orders and interprets tests, diagnoses and treats across primary, urgent and specialty care in collaboration with a physician. Recognises when a case needs escalation to the supervising physician.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, treatment, patient education, follow-up, and when you would involve the supervising physician

rubricEmphasis: Focused history, clinical reasoning, safe prescribing, knowing limits and escalating, patient education.

name: Nurse Practitioner
scope: Provides advanced nursing practice: comprehensive assessment, diagnosis, prescribing and management of acute and chronic conditions, with emphasis on health promotion, self-management and the patient's context.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: investigations, pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic treatment, health promotion, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Holistic assessment, diagnostic reasoning, safe prescribing, health promotion, self-management support.

name: Certified Nurse-Midwife
scope: Provides prenatal, postpartum, newborn-feeding, gynaecologic and family-planning care for low-risk patients, supports physiologic birth planning, screens for complications and perinatal mood disorders, and consults or refers when risk rises.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment: gestational age or postpartum day, risk status, problems identified
Plan: testing, education and anticipatory guidance, warning signs, consultation or referral, next visit

rubricEmphasis: Woman-centred care, screening for warning signs and perinatal depression, informed choice, appropriate consultation and referral.

name: Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA)
scope: Performs the pre-anaesthesia assessment and prepares patients for anaesthesia: airway, cardiopulmonary and sleep-apnoea risk, prior anaesthetic problems, medications, fasting instructions and the anaesthetic plan, in collaboration with the anaesthesia care team.

wrapUp.label: Risk assessment: ASA class, airway, aspiration, cardiopulmonary and other anaesthetic risks
Proposed anaesthetic plan and what was discussed with the patient
Pre-operative instructions: fasting, medications to hold or continue, items needing team review

rubricEmphasis: Systematic pre-anaesthesia assessment, identifying risks that change the plan, clear pre-operative instructions.

name: Nursing (RN)
scope: Performs a nursing assessment, monitors and interprets vital signs, identifies safety risks, provides patient education, and escalates concerns to the provider using SBAR.

wrapUp.label: Nursing assessment: priority findings and risks
Nursing interventions and patient education provided
SBAR to the provider (if escalation is needed)

rubricEmphasis: Systematic assessment, patient safety, recognition of deterioration, therapeutic communication, escalation.

name: Critical Care Nursing
scope: Tele-ICU and post-ICU nursing: monitors trends in vital signs and device data, recognises early deterioration, supports family communication, and follows up patients recovering at home after critical illness (weakness, delirium, tracheostomy or oxygen needs).

wrapUp.label: Nursing assessment: priority findings and risks
Nursing interventions and patient education provided
SBAR to the provider (if escalation is needed)

rubricEmphasis: Trend recognition, early warning scores, prioritisation, structured escalation, family-centred communication.

name: Emergency / Triage Nursing
scope: Telephone and video nurse triage: rapid focused assessment, acuity assignment using a validated scale, protocol-based advice, and directing the patient to the right level of care, including calling an ambulance.

wrapUp.label: Focused triage assessment and red flags identified
Acuity level and disposition (self-care, appointment, emergency department, ambulance) with reasoning
SBAR handoff to the receiving provider

rubricEmphasis: Rapid prioritisation, red-flag recognition, safe disposition, calm clear instructions, concise handoff.

name: Oncology / Infusion Nursing
scope: Supports patients receiving chemotherapy, immunotherapy and other cancer treatment: pre-treatment education, between-cycle symptom and toxicity assessment, central-line and self-care teaching, and urgent escalation of problems such as neutropenic fever.

wrapUp.label: Symptom and toxicity assessment (with grades) and psychosocial findings
Nursing interventions and self-care teaching provided
SBAR to the oncology provider (if escalation is needed)

rubricEmphasis: Toxicity grading, recognising oncologic emergencies, teach-back, emotional support, timely escalation.

name: Pediatric Nursing
scope: Nursing assessment and teaching for children and their caregivers: hydration, breathing and pain assessment by video, medication and device teaching (inhalers, insulin, feeding tubes), developmental and safety screening, and escalation of the sick child.

wrapUp.label: Nursing assessment: priority findings and risks
Nursing interventions and patient education provided
SBAR to the provider (if escalation is needed)

rubricEmphasis: Family-centred care, age-appropriate communication, recognising the sick child, weight-based medication safety, teach-back.

name: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
scope: Builds a therapeutic relationship, assesses mental status, mood, safety and medication effects, provides psychoeducation and coping support, and escalates risk. Tele-visits include medication monitoring and post-discharge check-ins.
noteFormat: Nursing note with mental status + SBAR

wrapUp.label: Mental status, safety assessment and medication effects
Nursing interventions, psychoeducation and safety planning
SBAR to the psychiatric provider (if escalation is needed)

rubricEmphasis: Therapeutic communication, suicide risk screening, side-effect monitoring, de-escalation, recovery-oriented language.

name: Community / Public Health Nursing
scope: Works with individuals and families in the community: home-visit style assessment by video, immunisation and communicable-disease follow-up including contact tracing, maternal-child health, health education and connection to community resources.
noteFormat: Nursing note / public health case record

wrapUp.label: Assessment of the individual, household and environment; risks identified
Education, interventions and referrals to community resources
Follow-up plan and any reporting or notification required

rubricEmphasis: Social determinants of health, cultural humility, health education, confidentiality in contact tracing, linkage to resources.

name: Nurse Case Management / Care Coordination
scope: Coordinates care across settings for patients with complex needs: transition-of-care calls after discharge, medication and appointment reconciliation, identifying barriers (cost, transport, caregiving), arranging services and equipment, and preventing readmission.
noteFormat: Case management assessment and care plan

wrapUp.label: Needs assessment: clinical status, understanding of the plan, barriers and readmission risk
Care plan: services, equipment and referrals arranged; who is responsible for each
Follow-up schedule and escalation triggers

rubricEmphasis: Barrier identification, medication and appointment reconciliation, advocacy, teach-back, interprofessional coordination.

name: Clinical Pharmacy
scope: Conducts comprehensive medication reviews and medication therapy management: best possible medication history, identification of drug therapy problems (indication, effectiveness, safety, adherence), monitoring of labs and levels, and recommendations to the prescriber. Includes anticoagulation and chronic-disease collaborative practice.
noteFormat: Pharmacist SOAP / MTM note with drug therapy problem list

wrapUp.label: Best possible medication history: discrepancies found
Drug therapy problems, prioritised (indication, effectiveness, safety, adherence)
Recommendations to the prescriber, patient education and monitoring plan

rubricEmphasis: Complete medication history including OTC and herbal products, interaction and dose checking, adherence exploration, clear prescriber recommendations.

name: Community Pharmacy
scope: Counsels patients on new and refill prescriptions, device technique, over-the-counter and self-care choices, and immunisations; screens for interactions and red flags that need referral to a prescriber; supports adherence and affordability.

wrapUp.label: Assessment: medication-related problems or self-care triage findings
Counselling provided and how understanding was confirmed
Recommendation (OTC product, refer to prescriber, pharmacist intervention) and follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Three prime questions, teach-back, OTC triage and referral red flags, interaction screening, plain language.

name: Physical Therapy
scope: Examines movement, strength, balance, pain and function; screens for red flags needing medical referral; establishes a physical therapy diagnosis and prognosis; prescribes and progresses exercise and teaches self-management. By video, tests are patient-performed under guidance.
noteFormat: PT evaluation (examination, evaluation, PT diagnosis, prognosis, plan of care with goals)

wrapUp.label: Examination findings: impairments, activity limitations, outcome measure scores
PT diagnosis, contributing factors, prognosis and any red flags
Short- and long-term functional goals (measurable, time-bound)
Plan of care: interventions, home exercise program, frequency and duration

rubricEmphasis: Red-flag screening, movement analysis, standardised outcome measures, functional goal writing, exercise dosing, patient education.

name: Occupational Therapy
scope: Builds an occupational profile and analyses performance of daily activities (self-care, home management, work, school, leisure); assesses cognition, upper-limb function and the home environment by video; recommends adaptations, equipment and strategies.
noteFormat: OT evaluation (occupational profile, analysis of occupational performance, goals, plan)

wrapUp.label: Occupational profile: roles, routines, priorities and environment
Analysis of occupational performance: what limits participation
Client-centred, measurable goals
Intervention plan: adaptations, equipment, strategies, caregiver training

rubricEmphasis: Client-centred goal setting, activity analysis, home safety, adaptive strategies, caregiver involvement.

name: Speech-Language Pathology
scope: Assesses and treats speech, language, cognitive-communication, voice, fluency and swallowing disorders in children and adults. By video: case history, screening and standardised tasks, swallowing history with caregiver-observed intake, and counselling on strategies.
noteFormat: SLP evaluation report (history, assessment results, diagnosis, goals, recommendations)

wrapUp.label: Assessment findings: communication and/or swallowing
Diagnostic impression and severity
Recommendations: goals, therapy plan, strategies for patient and family, referrals

rubricEmphasis: Thorough case history, appropriate task selection, aspiration red flags, family coaching, functional communication goals.

name: Audiology
scope: Evaluates hearing and balance complaints, interprets audiograms and tympanometry, counsels on hearing loss and its communication impact, fits and troubleshoots hearing aids remotely, and refers for medical evaluation when red flags are present.

wrapUp.label: Case history and audiologic findings (type, degree, configuration of hearing loss)
Communication impact and patient goals
Recommendations: amplification, communication strategies, medical referral, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Audiogram interpretation, medical-referral red flags (asymmetry, sudden loss), counselling on stigma, communication-partner strategies.

name: Respiratory Therapy
scope: Assesses breathing and oxygenation, teaches inhaler, nebuliser and airway-clearance technique, manages home oxygen, CPAP/BiPAP and home ventilation equipment, supports pulmonary rehabilitation and action plans, and escalates respiratory deterioration.
encounterTypes: COPD or asthma action plan review

wrapUp.label: Respiratory assessment: symptoms, oximetry, device data, technique errors observed
Interventions and teaching provided; equipment changes recommended
Findings to report to the prescriber and action-plan triggers

rubricEmphasis: Observed device technique with teach-back, oximetry interpretation, equipment troubleshooting, recognising exacerbation.

name: Dietetics / Clinical Nutrition
scope: Conducts nutrition assessment (diet history, anthropometrics, labs, barriers), makes a nutrition diagnosis, and delivers patient-centred nutrition education and counselling using motivational interviewing.

wrapUp.label: Nutrition assessment: key findings
Nutrition diagnosis (PES statement)
Intervention, patient goals agreed, monitoring and evaluation

rubricEmphasis: Motivational interviewing, cultural humility, plain-language education, realistic goal setting.

name: Clinical Psychology
scope: Conducts diagnostic clinical interviews, administers and interprets standardised measures, develops a case formulation, and delivers evidence-based psychotherapy such as CBT. Assesses risk and does not prescribe medication.
noteFormat: Psychological intake / progress note (presenting problem, MSE, formulation, treatment plan)

wrapUp.label: Presenting problem, relevant history and mental status
Case formulation and diagnostic impression
Risk assessment and safety plan
Treatment plan: modality, goals, measures, frequency

rubricEmphasis: Therapeutic alliance, structured assessment, case formulation, risk assessment, collaborative goal setting.

name: Clinical Social Work
scope: Completes a biopsychosocial assessment, identifies social needs (housing, food, finances, caregiving, safety), provides supportive counselling and crisis intervention, plans discharges, links to resources, and fulfils safeguarding and mandated reporting duties.

wrapUp.label: Biopsychosocial assessment: strengths, needs, supports and risks
Safety and safeguarding concerns (abuse, neglect, self-harm) and actions taken
Intervention plan: counselling, referrals, resources, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Person-in-environment perspective, strengths-based practice, safety screening, advocacy, self-determination.

name: Mental Health Counseling
scope: Provides talk therapy for mood, anxiety, grief, relationship, adjustment and life-transition concerns: intake assessment, goal setting, evidence-based counselling techniques, risk screening, and referral when needs exceed scope.
noteFormat: Intake assessment / DAP progress note (Data, Assessment, Plan)

wrapUp.label: Data: presenting concerns and what the client shared
Assessment: clinical impression, risk, stage of change
Plan: goals agreed, interventions, homework, next session

rubricEmphasis: Core counselling skills (reflection, open questions, validation), alliance, risk screening, culturally responsive practice.

name: Addiction / Substance Use Counseling
scope: Screens and assesses substance use and its consequences, determines stage of change and level-of-care needs, uses motivational interviewing, plans relapse prevention and harm reduction, and coordinates with medical providers for withdrawal risk and medication treatment.
noteFormat: Substance use assessment (ASAM dimensions) and treatment plan

wrapUp.label: Substance use history, consequences, stage of change and withdrawal or overdose risk
Level-of-care recommendation and reasoning
Treatment plan: goals in the client's words, harm reduction, relapse prevention, referrals

rubricEmphasis: Motivational interviewing spirit, non-stigmatising language, withdrawal and overdose risk recognition, harm reduction.

name: Medical Laboratory Science
scope: Patient-facing laboratory tele-visits: confirms identity and test orders, gives pre-collection instructions (fasting, timed and 24-hour collections, home and point-of-care testing), investigates pre-analytical problems behind implausible or rejected results, and explains what a test measures. Reports critical values to the ordering provider and does not diagnose or change treatment.

wrapUp.label: Pre-analytical findings: preparation, collection, interfering factors identified
Instructions given to the patient and how understanding was confirmed
What was reported to the ordering provider (including critical values) and recollection plan

rubricEmphasis: Two-identifier verification, pre-analytical variables, plain-language instructions, critical-value reporting, staying within scope.

name: Radiologic Technology / Medical Imaging
scope: Prepares patients for imaging: verifies identity and the order, screens for MRI safety (implants, metal), contrast risk (allergy, kidney function, metformin), pregnancy and claustrophobia, explains the examination and preparation, and flags concerns to the radiologist. Does not interpret images.
noteFormat: Imaging safety screening form and technologist note

wrapUp.label: Safety screening findings (implants, contrast risk, pregnancy, other)
Preparation instructions given and patient questions answered
Issues referred to the radiologist or ordering provider before the examination

rubricEmphasis: Systematic safety screening, patient identification, radiation and MRI safety explanation, easing anxiety, staying within scope.

name: Diagnostic Medical Sonography
scope: Prepares patients for ultrasound examinations: verifies the order and clinical indication, takes the focused history a sonographer needs, explains preparation (fasting, bladder filling) and what the scan involves including transvaginal consent, and explains that results come from the interpreting physician.

wrapUp.label: Focused clinical history relevant to the examination
Preparation and procedure explanation given; consent obtained
Information to pass to the interpreting physician

rubricEmphasis: Focused clinical history, dignity and consent for intimate examinations, managing requests for results, professional boundaries.

name: Genetic Counseling
scope: Takes a three-generation family history and draws a pedigree, assesses hereditary risk, explains inheritance and testing options with their limits and implications for relatives, supports informed decisions, and discloses and interprets genetic test results.
noteFormat: Genetic counseling summary (pedigree, risk assessment, testing plan)

wrapUp.label: Family history summary and pedigree interpretation
Risk assessment and inheritance pattern
Testing options discussed, the patient's decision, psychosocial issues, implications for relatives, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Accurate pedigree, non-directive counselling, risk communication with numbers, informed consent, psychosocial support.

name: Dentistry
scope: Teledentistry: triages dental pain, swelling, trauma and oral lesions; takes a medical and dental history including anticoagulants and bisphosphonates; inspects by camera and submitted photos; reviews radiographs; and decides urgency and interim management before in-chair treatment.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Dental diagnosis / differential and urgency
Plan: interim management, analgesia or antibiotics with justification, in-chair treatment needed, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Recognising spreading infection and airway risk, antibiotic stewardship, medical-dental interactions, pain management, anxiety.

name: Dental Hygiene
scope: Assesses oral health risk (caries, periodontal disease, oral cancer risk factors), reviews medical history and medications that affect the mouth, teaches oral hygiene technique, and counsels on diet, tobacco and prevention. Refers findings needing diagnosis to the dentist.
noteFormat: Dental hygiene process of care note (ADPIED)

wrapUp.label: Assessment: risk factors and oral findings
Dental hygiene diagnosis
Care plan: self-care instruction, preventive measures, referral to the dentist, recall interval

rubricEmphasis: Risk assessment, behaviour-change counselling, technique teaching with demonstration, oral-systemic links, appropriate referral.

name: Optometry
scope: Takes ocular and visual history, triages red eye and vision changes, manages refractive and contact-lens problems, dry eye, and follow-up of diabetic eye disease and glaucoma within scope. Recognises conditions needing urgent ophthalmology referral.

wrapUp.label: One-line summary of the patient
Assessment and differential diagnosis (most likely first, with reasoning)
Plan: treatment, lens advice, urgency and destination of referral, follow-up

rubricEmphasis: Ocular red flags, contact-lens hygiene counselling, explaining findings, timely referral.

name: Paramedicine / EMS
scope: Community paramedicine and telehealth-supported pre-hospital care: scene and primary survey, focused history (SAMPLE, OPQRST), vital signs and point-of-care tests, protocol-based treatment, transport versus treat-in-place decisions, and radio or handover reports.

wrapUp.label: Primary and secondary assessment findings and field impression
Treatment given under protocol and the patient's response
Transport decision and handover report to the receiving clinician

rubricEmphasis: Structured primary survey, time-critical recognition, protocol adherence, capacity and refusal assessment, concise handover.

name: Athletic Training
scope: Evaluates sports injuries and illness in athletes, manages concussion with graded return-to-sport and return-to-learn, designs rehabilitation and prevention programmes, and refers to a physician when red flags are present.
noteFormat: Injury evaluation (HOPS: History, Observation, Palpation, Special tests) / SOAP

wrapUp.label: Evaluation findings (history, observation, patient-guided palpation and special tests)
Clinical impression and red flags
Plan: treatment and rehabilitation, return-to-play stage and criteria, referral

rubricEmphasis: Mechanism of injury, concussion symptom assessment, return-to-play criteria, athlete and coach pressure, physician referral.

name: Health Coaching / Community Health Work
scope: Builds trust with patients in their own context, screens for social needs (food, housing, transport, cost of care), supports behaviour change with patient-chosen goals, navigates the health system and community resources, and relays concerns to the care team. Does not diagnose or give medication advice.

wrapUp.label: Needs and barriers identified, and strengths and supports
Goals in the patient's own words and action steps agreed
Resources and referrals made; what was communicated to the care team; next contact

rubricEmphasis: Trust and cultural humility, motivational interviewing, SMART goal setting, resource navigation, knowing when to hand off to a clinician.
